sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Jefferson County, Colorado?
sections.html:
Two county offices split the work. The Assessor sets value and hears appeals, and the Treasurer sends the bills and collects the money. Both are in the Jefferson County Administration and Courts building at 100 Jefferson County Parkway in Golden.

OfficeSuite and phoneRole
Assessor303-271-6511Value, classification, appeals
TreasurerSuite 2520, 303-271-8330Tax notices, payments, lien sale
Public TrusteeSuite 2510, 303-271-8580Deed of trust releases, foreclosures

The Treasurer's counter is open Monday through Thursday, 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., and closed on Fridays. The Treasurer cannot raise or lower a bill. The amount comes from three pieces: the Assessor's value and classification, assessment rates set by the state General Assembly, and mill levies set by each taxing entity.

sections.h2: What is Jefferson County like for a homeowner?
sections.html:
Jefferson County runs along the Front Range next to Denver and covers about 774 square miles. Golden is the county seat, Lakewood is the largest city, and the county was reorganized on November 1, 1861 as one of Colorado Territory's original 17.

Cities in the county include Arvada (part), Edgewater, Golden, Lakewood, Littleton (part), Westminster (part), Wheat Ridge, Morrison and Superior (part). Mountain communities such as Conifer and Pine are unincorporated. Your address decides which city, fire district and school district levies show up on the tax notice.

The job base includes the Coors brewery in Golden, the Colorado School of Mines, and the Denver Federal Center in Lakewood, which Wikipedia describes as the largest concentration of federal agencies outside Washington, D.C. Owners near those employers and along the foothills often have very different lots, from small bungalows to acreage in the canyons.

sections.h2: When are Jefferson County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Property tax in Colorado is paid in arrears, so 2025 taxes were payable in 2026. The Treasurer mails notices in late January and the coupons are attached.

2026 payment dateWhat it covers
March 2, 2026First half. February 28 fell on a Saturday, so the county moved the date.
April 30, 2026Full year in one payment
June 15, 2026Second half

U.S. postmarks are accepted for the February, April and June deadlines. When the end of February, April or June lands on a Friday or weekend, the county accepts payment the next business day without delinquent interest. Online payments can take several days to leave your bank account, so do not wait for the last minute.

sections.h2: What happens after a Jefferson County tax bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate taxes are advertised in the fall and then sold as a lien to an investor in November. Delinquent notices are mailed in July, and in August a tax buyer holding an older lien can pay the current year, which adds to that certificate.

  • Early October: the first of three weekly newspaper notices for unpaid real property taxes. The county also says delinquent taxes are advertised for three consecutive weeks beginning in September, and that paying before September 1 avoids the advertising charge.
  • November: the annual tax lien sale, run as an internet sale.
  • Redemption: the owner has three years to redeem the lien by paying the delinquent tax plus accrued interest.
  • After three years: the certificate holder may apply for a public auction of a certificate of option for a treasurer's deed.

Redemption payments must reach the office by 5 p.m. on the last business day of the month, in cash or certified funds. Postmarks do not count, and interest accrues monthly. Call 303-271-8330 for a payoff figure.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Jefferson County property valuation?
sections.html:
You file with the Assessor between May 1 and June 8, and any mailed appeal must be postmarked by June 8. The county advises filing early because the last days are busy.

  1. Read the Notice of Valuation mailed on May 1 and check value and classification.
  2. Research comparable sales in the Property Records Search, or call 303-271-8666 about inventory for up to three residences.
  3. File the appeal form, mail it, or book an appraiser appointment online.
  4. Expect a Notice of Determination by August 15.
  5. If you still disagree, file with the Board of Equalization by September 15.
  6. The Board must finish hearings by November 1 and notify petitioners within five business days.
  7. A Board decision can be appealed within 30 days.

The dates in steps four through six come from the county's appeal page, which differs from the statewide calendar shown by some other counties, so confirm them with the Assessor if your deadline is close.

sections.h2: How is the current valuation cycle set?
sections.html:
Jefferson County's last reappraisal was 2025, and tax year 2026 is an intervening year. Owners whose value did not change generally did not get a full notice. Postcard notices of value in 2026 went only to owners with changes such as new construction.

The valuation date for this cycle is June 30, 2024, and the Assessor looked only at sales from July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2024. A sale after that date will not show up in the 2025 and 2026 values, so a house that sold higher or lower later is still valued from the earlier data.

sections.h2: What do I need to know about the lien and tax rules when selling?
sections.html:
Because taxes are paid in arrears, a sale that closes in 2026 still leaves a 2026 tax bill that arrives in January 2027. Ask your title or escrow company how that bill will be split, and make sure any past due balance is cleared first.

  • Confirm there is no unpaid balance from earlier years, since a buyer's title search will find a tax lien.
  • Ask the Treasurer about the prepayment cutoff: next year's taxes can be prepaid until noon on the last business day of December.
  • Check whether a Public Trustee release is needed for an old loan.
  • If you are mailing a payment, use certified funds for lien redemption.

sections.h2: How do wildfire rules affect selling a mountain home in Jefferson County?
sections.html:
The Wildfire Resiliency Code, approved March 10, 2026 and effective July 1, 2026, applies to unincorporated properties in the wildland urban interface. It reaches new construction and exterior alterations, including re-roofing and re-siding, and it is not retroactive.

A roof replacement of 25% or more must be a Class A assembly. Defensible space must be inspected by a county approved Wildfire Mitigation Specialist. Re-siding projects that call for Zone 1 standards may use a self-attestation form.

For sellers, that can add cost to a repair list in Conifer, Pine or the foothills. Reading the county's defensible space page before you hire a roofer saves surprises.

sections.h2: Does a cash sale change the tax picture?
sections.html: A cash sale does not change what is owed to the Treasurer. Any unpaid taxes, a lien or a mortgage balance still has to be settled at or before closing, so an offer from a direct buyer works best when you know your payoff numbers first.

faqs.q: When is the Jefferson County, CO property tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Appeals to the Assessor are due by June 8, with mailed appeals postmarked that day. The window opens May 1 when notices of valuation go out.

faqs.q: When are Jefferson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, the first half was due March 2, the full year April 30 and the second half June 15. Notices mail in late January.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Jefferson County taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. Colorado allows payment in two halves or one full payment, and the county's Important Dates page lists the February, April and June deadlines. The county's tax billing page itself does not describe installments, so confirm with the Treasurer.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem a Jefferson County tax lien?
faqs.a: The county says the owner has three years to redeem a tax lien by paying the delinquent taxes and accrued interest. Call 303-271-8330 for the payoff amount.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Jefferson County property value?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor at 303-271-6511. The Treasurer at 303-271-8330 can explain payments but cannot change a bill.
